messages.content: The client moved Tuesday's first session to 9:00 a.m., so the Tuesday flight is out. Monday lodging is approved. Can you put the Monday Delta flight and the Hampton together and check the full cost before I buy either one?

Yes. I have the Monday itinerary at $548 round trip and the Hampton for four nights at $179 per night. I’ll verify that the arrival works with the new start, then reconcile taxes, payment timing, and the restrictive terms. Is the $548 fare showing as Main Cabin or Basic Economy in your cart?
Main Cabin. It says MSP 7:05 p.m. to RDU 10:38 p.m. Monday, then RDU 5:35 p.m. to MSP 7:24 p.m. Friday.

That resolves the schedule issue. Even allowing about 15 minutes to get off the aircraft and 35 to 50 minutes for a rideshare to Cary, you should reach the hotel around 11:30 p.m. Monday. You’ll have the full night before Tuesday’s 9:00 a.m. session.

The airfare is $548 including airline taxes and fees. Main Cabin is nonrefundable, but it can generally be changed without a change fee; any fare increase would still be due. If you cancel before departure, the ticket value is normally issued as an eCredit rather than returned to the corporate card. One personal item and one carry-on are included, but a checked bag is not.
I’ll have one carry-on, no checked bag. What does the hotel come to with tax?

The room calculation is:

Four nights at $179: $716.00
Estimated hotel taxes at 13.25%: $94.87
Estimated hotel total: $810.87

Combined with the $548 airfare, the trip total is $1,358.87. That excludes rideshares, meals beyond the included breakfast, and any incidental authorization the hotel places on the card.
Is that hotel tax confirmed or just an estimate?

It is the tax currently displayed for the Hampton rate, but the hotel labels taxes as subject to change before the stay. The booking screen’s payable estimate is $810.87, with the room charged at the property rather than now.
And the cancellation cutoff is still Sunday night?

Yes. The rate remains cancellable without charge through Sunday, October 12 at 11:59 p.m. in the hotel’s local time. A cancellation after that point, or a no-show, carries a one-night room-and-tax penalty, currently about $202.72. There is no advance room payment, but a card is required to guarantee the reservation.
Since the flight lands late, will they treat me as a no-show before I get there?

No. A 10:38 p.m. landing should still put you at the hotel before midnight, and the card guarantee holds the room for late arrival. I can include the flight arrival time in the reservation note. If the flight becomes severely delayed and arrival slips well past midnight, calling the front desk would still be prudent.
Please add the late-arrival note. Also, does the return flight leave enough room after the final client meeting? It ends at 3:00 in Cary.

Yes. Leaving the client site around 3:20 should put you at RDU around 4:00 to 4:15 under ordinary Friday traffic, about 80 to 95 minutes before the 5:35 departure. Since you are carrying on only, that is workable. A significant meeting overrun or traffic disruption would reduce the margin, so I would avoid departing the site later than about 3:35.
That’s fine. Keep the Friday flight. Can you verify the hotel dates one more time? I don’t want the extra Monday night to shift checkout accidentally.

The hotel dates are correct: check in Monday, October 13, and check out Friday, October 17. That is four nights: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Friday is the checkout and return-flight day; there is no Friday-night room charge.
Good. My traveler profile has my legal name and date of birth, and the corporate card ending in 1842 is ready. Do you need anything else from me before these are ready to purchase?

I need two confirmations from the checkout details: does the traveler profile show the same legal name as your government ID, and is the billing address attached to the card ending in 1842 current? Please don’t send the full card number or security code in chat.
Yes to both. The loyalty number in the profile is also correct. Use that card for the flight guarantee and the hotel guarantee.

Understood. I have the traveler profile attached to the flight and the card ending in 1842 selected for both transactions. The hotel will use it only as a guarantee now and is expected to charge the stay at the property. The airfare would be charged immediately when purchased.
Give me the final review, including anything I would be agreeing to, but stop before the purchase step.

Purchase-ready review:

Flight: Delta Main Cabin, Monday, October 13, MSP 7:05 p.m. to RDU 10:38 p.m.; Friday, October 17, RDU 5:35 p.m. to MSP 7:24 p.m. Round-trip total: $548.00, charged at purchase. The ticket is nonrefundable; voluntary changes may require a fare difference, and cancellation before departure generally produces an eCredit. Carry-on and personal item are included; no checked bag is included.

Hotel: Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh/Cary-I-40, standard king, October 13 through October 17, four nights. Room subtotal: $716.00. Estimated taxes: $94.87. Estimated hotel total: $810.87, payable at the property, with a possible incidental hold. Free cancellation ends October 12 at 11:59 p.m. hotel local time; the late-cancellation or no-show penalty is one night plus tax, currently about $202.72. The reservation note states that you expect a late arrival following a 10:38 p.m. flight.

Estimated combined total: $1,358.87. The Monday arrival supports the Tuesday 9:00 a.m. client start, and the Friday return remains workable after the 3:00 p.m. meeting. Both items are staged with the traveler profile and corporate card ending in 1842, but no charge or reservation has been submitted.
